decisions.reason: As a core-category safety shoe line that has remained available into 2025, it still looks like a viable option for this firm and is unlikely to be withdrawn unless specific models have clearly underperformed.

The comfort insole is a low-cost complementary add-on to the footwear business, so management would likely keep it while continuing to learn demand, even though overlap with other insoles creates some pruning risk.

After two selling cycles, the supportive insole appears the most vulnerable overlapping option in a crowded insole set, so real-options logic favors closing this weaker variant and reallocating attention to clearer bets.
The ergonomic safety shoe series fits the firm’s innovation and premium-protective-footwear positioning closely, so its continued retention is the more likely choice.

Firefighter and rescue boots serve a narrower niche, but they are adjacent to the firm’s protective-footwear capabilities and may warrant more time because specialized demand can take longer to reveal itself.
Because the moulded insole was presented as a flagship direction, management would be very unlikely to abandon it quickly and would instead continue building on it as a strategic option.
